original_test_intent: Verify that the owner-approved stored User Defaults profile can be recalled through Restore User Defaults and that the intended profile values become the pending or applied configuration, while the source Criteria only test whether a setting can be saved.
original_method: Capture the current operational profile, identify the stored user-default profile, invoke Restore User Defaults in BIOS, compare recalled values with the approved profile, save/activate only if documented and approved, then restore the required final configuration.
manual_activity: A human must identify the profile, select Restore User Defaults, inspect the recalled firmware values and perform any separately approved save/activation. Automated readback cannot exercise or observe the BIOS control itself.
required_inputs: Approved stored User Defaults identity and expected field matrix
Console/operator, OOB recovery and final profile
safety_requirements: Do not restore an unidentified, stale or unapproved profile.
Capture the current boot/storage/security/management configuration before recall.
Do not assume recalled values are active until platform semantics prove it.
Require separate approval before save, reset or reboot if those steps are needed.
Stop on unexpected field delta or boot/management risk.
Restore the approved final profile and do not retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Collect identity, baseline, profile and health evidence and compare field matrices.
Highlight the source criterion gap and pending-versus-active state.
Do not operate firmware UI, approve activation or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Accept or correct a recall/application criterion aligned with the named function.
Approve the profile, activation boundary, recovery and final state.
Perform/capture the restore action and determine the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its interpretation of Restore User Defaults as profile recall is technically aligned with Items, but the source Criteria do not establish that recall/application is the required PASS condition.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the actual interactive Restore User Defaults control and field comparison; do not substitute a configuration import, generic save or the preceding Save as User Defaults operation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Restore User Defaults, save-only Criteria, no-script state and 5/5-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RECALL STATE TRACE WITH CRITERION CORRECTION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After the owner accepts a recall criterion, record current and stored-profile matrices, invoke Restore User Defaults manually, distinguish pending from committed values, activate only as documented and approved, verify the selected profile and health, then restore the final operational state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact board and BIOS user-default implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC and profile-capture format versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform Restore User Defaults and activation semantics.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds profile identity, field comparison and state transitions and explicitly identifies that saving alone cannot prove recall.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preserves restore coverage and treats save/activation as a platform-dependent supporting step rather than the acceptance target.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Corrected/accepted criterion, profile matrix and activation behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Unknown or stale profiles can change boot-critical settings; hidden fields may require owner disposition.

project_override_considerations: The project selects the approved profile, activation method and final state. It may supplement the Criteria with recall/application evidence but must record the Master Source's save-only wording and cannot report that saving alone proves restore.
expected_evidence: Source-gap disposition, identity, approval and recovery plan
Current baseline and approved stored-profile matrix
Restore User Defaults action and pending-value comparison
Any separately approved save/activation plus applied values and health
Restored final profile and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items name Restore User Defaults, which requires evidence that a stored profile is recalled/applied; Criteria only ask whether a setting can be saved. Saving is neither unique to nor sufficient proof of the restore function.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation intent remains clear from the named control and DeepSeek interpretation. The criterion gap requires owner disposition before formal execution, but it does not make the technical operation itself ambiguous enough to classify the library case as permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its manual profile-recall interpretation but records the missing acceptance alignment.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains profile identity, baseline, comparison, recovery and its criterion concern while separating classification from readiness.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records a real coverage mismatch without collapsing a clear manual function into BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a generic save confirmation from being accepted as evidence that the stored profile was actually recalled and applied.
independent_technical_reasoning: Restore User Defaults is identifiable and inherently interactive, so MANUAL ONLY describes its core execution. The save-only Criteria are materially misaligned but do not reverse or obscure which BIOS control is being tested; they are recorded as SOURCE_CONFLICT plus readiness disposition rather than BLOCKED.
no_automatic_retry: Do not repeat recall, save or activation after an unexpected profile delta or ambiguous state; preserve the first transition evidence and obtain engineer disposition.
